title: HB2896 (2022 Regular Session): Changes the law regarding retired law enforcement officers carrying concealed weapons

provenance.fetched_by: LegiScan bulk dataset (gun-policy Stage 5 LegiScan check); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official house.mo.gov or senate.mo.gov PDF of the version named in note (via LegiScan getBillText)

operative_text:
Section 650.030 (RSMo): 1. The director of public safety shall establish a state firearms training and qualification standard for retired law enforcement officers carrying concealed firearms pursuant to 18 U.S.C. 926C of the Law Enforcement Officers Safety Act of 2004 and shall promulgate rules for the implementation of this state standard as required by 18 U.S.C. Section 926C(d)(2)(B).
Section 650.030 (RSMo): 2. A retired law enforcement officer satisfies the federal certification requirements if he or she possesses a valid firearms qualification certificate that: (1) Uses the model certificate created under subsection 4 of this section; (2) Provides that either a law enforcement agency or an individual or entity certified to provide firearms training acknowledges that the bearer has been found qualified or otherwise found to satisfy the standards established by the peace officer standards and training commission for firearms qualification for the basic training of peace officers; and (3) Complies with the time restrictions provided under subsection 3 of this section.
Section 650.030 (RSMo): 3. The firearms certificate is valid for a period of one year from the date that the law enforcement agency, individual, or entity certified to provide firearms training determines that the bearer is qualified or otherwise found to satisfy the standards established by the peace officer standards and training commission for firearms qualification for the basic training of peace officers, and the certificate shall state the date the determination was made.
Section 650.030 (RSMo): 5. The retired law enforcement officer is responsible for paying the costs of the firearms qualification required under subsection 2 of this section.
Section 650.030 (RSMo): 6. Nothing in this section shall be deemed to require a local law enforcement agency to complete the certificate.
